summary: Fluticasone propionate is a potent topical corticosteroid used intranasally for allergic rhinitis. Adults and children >=12 use 2 sprays per nostril once daily for week 1, then 1-2 sprays per nostril as needed. Minimal systemic absorption; key cautions are nasal septal effects and growth in children.
indications: Temporary relief of nasal symptoms of hay fever and upper respiratory allergies (nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, itchy nose)
Itchy, watery eyes associated with allergic rhinitis

dosage.d: 2 sprays in each nostril once daily
1-2 sprays in each nostril once daily as needed
1 spray in each nostril once daily

admin: Prime the bottle before first use and shake gently before each use
Use only once daily; do not exceed directed dose
Direct spray away from the nasal septum
Full benefit may take several days of regular use
moa: A synthetic corticosteroid with high affinity for the glucocorticoid receptor. Binding suppresses transcription of pro-inflammatory cytokines and mediators, reducing infiltration of inflammatory cells (eosinophils, mast cells) and decreasing nasal mucosal inflammation, secretion and hyperresponsiveness in allergic rhinitis.

relative: Recent nasal surgery, trauma or septal ulcers
monitor: Concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir, ketoconazole)

preg: Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed. Intranasal corticosteroids have low systemic exposure; lowest effective dose is recommended.
lact: Caution advised; systemic exposure from intranasal use is low and infant exposure is expected to be minimal. Weigh benefit against potential risk.
renal: No dose adjustment required given low systemic absorption.
hepatic: Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment, as reduced clearance may increase systemic corticosteroid exposure.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, ketoconazole) - markedly increased systemic fluticasone, risk of Cushing syndrome / adrenal suppression
moderate: Other corticosteroids (any route) - additive systemic corticosteroid effects
interactions.diagnostics: High-dose chronic use may suppress HPA axis (cortisol).

serious: Glaucoma or cataract with prolonged use
rare: Impaired wound healing in nasal mucosa
emergency: Severe allergic reaction / angioedema or anaphylaxis

pearls: Intranasal route gives high local potency with low systemic bioavailability

missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered, then resume once-daily dosing. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Acute overdose via the intranasal route is unlikely to produce clinically significant effects. Chronic excessive use may cause systemic corticosteroid effects (HPA-axis suppression); manage by reducing dose.
